sentences.en: For many people, this is what work sounds like nowadays.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这就是如今工作时的声音。

sentences.en: It's a constant thrum of notifications, tweets, and messages.
sentences.zh: 充斥着源源不断的通知、推特和消息。

sentences.en: Every time we respond to an email or a text,
sentences.zh: 每当我们回复电子邮件或短信，

sentences.en: or Google a question that's just popped into our head,
sentences.zh: 或者用谷歌搜索刚刚在脑海中闪过的问题时，
我们都要付出一点小小的代价。

sentences.en: In the moment, this price is imperceptible.
sentences.zh: 眼下，这个代价是察觉不到的。

sentences.en: But over time, it adds up.
sentences.zh: 但日积月累，它就会累积起来。

sentences.en: And we haven't quite come to terms with the cost of constant distraction.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还没有完全意识到持续分心所带来的代价。

sentences.en: We treat it, I think, in this more general sense of,
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们对它的普遍看法是，

sentences.en: I probably should be less distracted.
sentences.zh: 我可能应该少分心一点。

sentences.en: And I think it's more urgent than people realize.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这件事比大家意识到的更为紧迫。

sentences.en: Today, we look at the challenge of cultivating deep attention
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来探讨培养深度注意力的挑战，

sentences.en: and what we gain by immersing ourselves in meaningful work.
sentences.zh: 以及沉浸于有意义的工作中能为我们带来什么。

sentences.en: I spoke to someone who might seem like an unlikely advocate
sentences.zh: 我采访了一位看似不太可能成为技术克制倡导者的人，

sentences.en: for technological restraint, a computer scientiSt.
Cal Newport is a computer science professor at Georgetown University.
sentences.zh: 卡尔·纽波特是乔治城大学的计算机科学教授。

sentences.en: He's deliberately tried to break away from the distractions of modern technology.
sentences.zh: 他一直在刻意尝试摆脱现代科技带来的干扰。

sentences.en: And he's trying to get the rest of us to follow his lead.
sentences.zh: 并试图让其余的人也效仿他的做法。

sentences.en: Cal is the author of Deep Work, Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World.
sentences.zh: 卡尔是《深度工作：如何在分心世界中取得成效》一书的作者。
卡尔，欢迎来到《隐秘大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Well, thanks for having me on.
You talk in your book about several highly influential thinkers,
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到了几位极具影响力的人物，

sentences.en: people like the psychiatrist Carl Jung,
sentences.zh: 比如精神病学家卡尔·荣格，

sentences.en: and you say they all have a set of habits that are quite striking
sentences.zh: 你说他们在能够出色完成工作方面，

sentences.en: in terms of how they're able to get great work done.
sentences.zh: 都有一套非常引人注目的习惯。

sentences.en: This was something I noticed was very common to influential thinkers,
sentences.zh: 这是我注意到在具有影响力的人物中非常普遍的一种现象，

sentences.en: is that they all seem to have this drive to, on a regular basis,
sentences.zh: 就是他们似乎都有这样一种冲动：定期

sentences.en: cut themselves off from their lives of busyness and communication and distraction
sentences.zh: 将自己与忙碌、社交和分心的生活隔离开来，

sentences.en: and isolate themselves to think deeply.
Well, what you'll notice is that they often will have a location,
sentences.zh: 你会发现，他们通常都会有一个地点，

sentences.en: a separate location they go to when they want to think deeply
sentences.zh: 一个当他们想要深度思考时会去的分开的地点，

sentences.en: that's often cut off from the rest of their life.
sentences.zh: 这个地点通常与他们生活的其余部分相隔绝。

sentences.en: So Carl Jung would go out to the Bollingen Tower,
sentences.zh: 所以卡尔·荣格会去博林根之塔，

sentences.en: a stone house without electricity or running water
sentences.zh: 那是一座没有电也没有自来水的石头房子，

sentences.en: he built by the lakeside outside of a small village
sentences.zh: 是他自己在苏黎世郊外一个小村庄旁边的

sentences.en: Rowling, when she was struggling to finish The Deathly Hallows,
sentences.zh: 罗琳在艰难创作《死亡圣器》快要完结时，

sentences.en: rented out this big suite at the Balmore Hotel
sentences.zh: 租下了巴尔莫勒尔酒店的一间大套房，

sentences.en: next to the big castle in downtown Edinburgh
sentences.zh: 就挨着爱丁堡市中心的大城堡，

sentences.en: where she'd go and just think Harry Potter-style thoughts.
sentences.zh: 她会在那里思考哈利·波特风格的问题。

sentences.en: Mark Twain had a cabin for a long period of his life
sentences.zh: 马克·吐温在其生活中的很长一段时间里，

sentences.en: he would go to on the property of their house.
sentences.zh: 在自家宅邸的地产上有一间小屋供他前往。

sentences.en: It was so far from the house that his family had to blow a horn
sentences.zh: 那个小屋离主宅太远了，以至于他的家人必须吹号角

sentences.en: to try to catch his attention and let him know that dinner was ready.
sentences.zh: 来引起他的注意，好让他知道晚饭准备好了。

sentences.en: They'd go somewhere physically isolated and different
sentences.zh: 他们会去到某个物理上隔离且不同的地方，

sentences.en: where they can, without distraction, think deeply.
sentences.zh: 在那里免受干扰地进行深度思考。

sentences.en: What does work look like for the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 我们其余人的工作状态又是怎样的呢？

sentences.en: When you look at the average American worker, for example,
sentences.zh: 比如，当你审视普通美国工人时，

sentences.en: are most of us doing this kind of deep, sustained work?
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人都在进行这种深入、持续的工作吗？

sentences.en: The type of deep work I talk about is almost non-existent,
sentences.zh: 据我所知，在我所讨论的绝大多数知识工作岗位中，

sentences.en: as far as I can tell, in most knowledge work positions.
sentences.zh: 这种深度工作几乎是不存在的。

sentences.en: Even when people think that they're single-tasking,
sentences.zh: 即使人们认为自己在单任务处理时，

sentences.en: they say, I've learned a lesson that I'm not supposed to multitask,
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我吸取了教训，我不应该多任务处理，

sentences.en: I'm not supposed to be on the phone and do email while I write,
sentences.zh: 我写作时既不应该接电话也不应该看邮件，

sentences.en: I'm just working on one thing at a time.
What they're still doing is every five or ten minutes a just check.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍在做的是，每隔五分钟或十分钟就“看一眼”。

sentences.en: Let me just do a just check to my inbox.
sentences.zh: 让我去收件箱看一眼就好。

sentences.en: Let me just do a just check to my phone real quick and then back to my work.
sentences.zh: 让我迅速看一眼手机，然后就回到工作中。
这感觉像是单任务处理。

sentences.en: It feels like you're predominantly working on one thing.
sentences.zh: 感觉你主要是在专心做一件事。

sentences.en: But even those very brief checks that switch your context even briefly
sentences.zh: 但即使是那些极短暂的、哪怕短暂改变你语境的查看，

sentences.en: can have this massive negative impact on your cognitive performance.
sentences.zh: 也会对你的认知表现产生巨大的负面影响。

sentences.en: It's the switch itself that hurts, not how long you actually switch.
sentences.zh: 有害的是切换本身，而不是你实际切换了多久。

sentences.en: So I actually think even very conscientious knowledge workers
sentences.zh: 所以我甚至认为，那些非常认真的知识工作者，

sentences.en: who think they're pretty good at focusing on one thing at a time
sentences.zh: 自以为很擅长一次专注做一件事的人，

sentences.en: are actually still working far from the sort of high-performance deep work ideal.
sentences.zh: 其实际工作状态离高性能深度工作的理想状态还相去甚远。

sentences.en: What is the evidence that this switching causes harm to the quality of your thinking?
sentences.zh: 有什么证据表明这种切换会损害你的思维质量？

sentences.en: Well, we've seen this show up in different types of scientific studies
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到这在不同类型的科学研究中

sentences.en: and from different types of perspectives.
sentences.zh: 以及从不同的角度显现出来。

sentences.en: I think one angle that makes it pretty clear is the work that
sentences.zh: 我认为有一个角度讲得很清楚，那就是

sentences.en: Professor Sophie Leroy has done on an effect called attention residue.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·勒鲁瓦教授针对一种名为“注意力残留”的效应所做的工作。

sentences.en: This is actually something that's pretty easy to isolate in the laboratory.
sentences.zh: 这实际上在实验室里是相当容易分离出来的。

sentences.en: You essentially give a subject something cognitively demanding to do
sentences.zh: 你基本上是给受试者一些需要消耗认知能力、

sentences.en: that you can measure, like trying to solve hard puzzles.
sentences.zh: 你可以进行测量的事情去做，比如尝试解开困难的谜题。

sentences.en: And then at some point, you distract them briefly as the experimenter,
sentences.zh: 然后作为实验人员，你在某个时刻短暂地打断他们，

sentences.en: have them look at something else, change their context very briefly.
sentences.zh: 让他们看别的东西，非常短暂地改变他们的语境。

sentences.en: When they then turn back to the original cognitively demanding task,
sentences.zh: 当他们随后转回原本那项需要消耗认知能力的任务时，
你会发现他们的表现下降了。

sentences.en: And it drops for a while.
sentences.zh: 而且这种下降会持续一段时间。

sentences.en: It takes a while for this attention residue to clear out.
sentences.zh: 这种注意力残留需要一段时间才能清除。

sentences.en: And this is essentially what we're doing to ourselves
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们在对收件箱或手机进行快速一瞥时，

sentences.en: when we do that quick glance at the inbox or to the phone.

sentences.zh: 我正在与卡尔·纽波特对话。

sentences.en: He's a computer science professor at Georgetown University
sentences.zh: 他是乔治城大学的计算机科学教授，

sentences.en: and the author of Deep Work, Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World.
sentences.zh: 也是《深度工作：如何在分心世界中取得成效》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Cal, I'm wondering, do you think most of us are aware of the costs of distraction in our lives?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，我想知道，你认为我们大多数人是否意识到了生活中分心的代价？

sentences.en: People, I think, intuit that they're too distracted
sentences.zh: 我认为人们有一种直觉，觉得自己分心太严重了，

sentences.en: and it's making them feel fragmented and exhausted and anxious.
sentences.zh: 这让他们感到碎片化、精疲力竭和焦虑。

sentences.en: But we treat it, I think, in this more general sense of,
sentences.zh: 但我们对待它的方式，我认为更偏向于这种笼统的看法：

sentences.en: I probably should be less distracted.
sentences.zh: 我大概应该少分心一点。

sentences.en: And I think it's more urgent than people realize that if your brain is how you make a living,
sentences.zh: 而我认为，这比人们意识到的更为紧迫，如果你的大脑是你谋生的工具，

sentences.en: then you really have to worry about this cognitive fitness.
sentences.zh: 那你真的必须关注这种认知的健康状况。

sentences.en: I mean, how are you getting performance out of your brain?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你是如何让你的大脑发挥出表现的？

sentences.en: Are you taking care to get good performance out of your brain or not?
sentences.zh: 你有没有用心让大脑保持良好的表现？

sentences.en: And people would probably be surprised, the more they think about it,
sentences.zh: 而且人们越去思考，可能就会越惊讶，

sentences.en: how much they're leaving on the table by the way they're currently working.
sentences.zh: 因为他们目前的工作方式，白白错失了多少潜力。

sentences.en: Does it matter that most of us are not trying to win a Nobel Prize or a Pulitzer Prize,
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人并不打算赢得诺贝尔奖或普利策奖，
我们不一定是天才，这重要吗？

sentences.en: Does it actually matter for most of us that we don't regularly put ourselves in a state of deep work?
sentences.zh: 我们没有经常让自己处于深度工作状态，这对我们大多数人来说真的重要吗？

sentences.en: Well, this is a big shift that I think has happened in our economy
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是我们经济中发生的一个巨大转变，

sentences.en: because it's an increasing portion of our economy that are essentially making a living
sentences.zh: 因为经济中越来越大的一部分人，基本上都是靠

sentences.en: by using their brain to process information and produce new information.
sentences.zh: 使用大脑来处理信息和产生新信息来谋生的。

sentences.en: And even if you're not trying to write great literature or solve a great theorem,
sentences.zh: 即使你不是在试图写出伟大的文学作品或解开伟大的定理，

sentences.en: if you're using your brain primarily to produce value,
sentences.zh: 如果你主要是在用大脑来创造价值，

sentences.en: be it writing marketing copy or putting together a new plan for your business startup,
sentences.zh: 无论是撰写营销文案还是为你的创业公司制定新计划，
这些类型的事情都很重要。

sentences.en: The human brain has become one of the main capital resources in our economy.
sentences.zh: 人类的大脑已经成为我们经济中的主要资本资源之一。

sentences.en: It's what in the knowledge economy we spend most of our money on
sentences.zh: 在知识经济中，我们把大部分资金都花在

sentences.en: is supporting human brains to process things and produce value.
sentences.zh: 支持人类大脑处理事情和创造价值上。
所以我们应该关心这一点。

sentences.en: I think the ability to do deep work would be relevant to the professional success
sentences.zh: 我认为进行深度工作的能力与几乎所有

sentences.en: of almost everyone in the knowledge work field, which is a huge part of our economy.
sentences.zh: 知识工作领域人员的职业成功息息相关，而这在我们经济中占了很大一部分。

sentences.en: I'd like to run a little thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 我想做一个小小的思想实验。

sentences.en: Imagine we're following a doctor as she's making the rounds of a hospital,
sentences.zh: 想象我们在跟随一位医生查房，

sentences.en: and she's looking at many patients,
and presumably the patients all present with different problems and complications and so forth.
sentences.zh: 想必这些病人都有不同的问题、并发症等等。

sentences.en: And I think what we would expect is for this doctor to very quickly flit from one subject,
sentences.zh: 我想我们会期望这位医生非常迅速地从一个对象、

sentences.en: one topic, one patient to the next.
sentences.zh: 一个主题、一个病人跳到下一个。

sentences.en: That if the doctor were to say, you know, I can only do my best work if I can focus on one patient,
sentences.zh: 如果医生说，你知道的，只有当我能专注一个病人、

sentences.en: deeply understand that case, spend a lot of time with it, yes, that might be true,
sentences.zh: 深入理解那个病例、花大量时间在上面时，我才能做到最好，是的，这或许是真的，

sentences.en: but it's going to come at a cost, which is all the other patients that the doctor is not going to see.
sentences.zh: 但它将伴随着一个代价，那就是医生将无法看到其他所有的病人。

sentences.en: What are the costs of deep work?
sentences.zh: 深度工作的代价是什么？

sentences.en: Well, where I'd want to get with the doctor is just the ability,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想从医生身上探讨的仅仅是这种能力：

sentences.en: even if you're relatively briefly staying with each patient,
sentences.zh: 即使你在每个病人身上停留的时间相对较短，

sentences.en: to actually be able to stay just with that patient.
sentences.zh: 也能真正做到只专注在那一个病人身上。

sentences.en: So a case study I uncovered actually after the book came out
sentences.zh: 所以我实际上在书出版后发现的一个案例研究是，

sentences.en: was of two different groups at the same elite level residency.
sentences.zh: 同一顶尖水平住院医师培训项目中的两个不同群体。

sentences.en: One group had a culture of email.
sentences.zh: 其中一个群体有一种电子邮件文化。

sentences.en: So, hey, I need something, here's a question, what about this patient?
sentences.zh: 所以，嘿，我需要点东西，这里有个问题，这个病人怎么样？

sentences.en: And they're expected to constantly be available by email.
sentences.zh: 并且他们被期望随时通过电子邮件保持联络。

sentences.en: The other group consolidated that type of administrative or logistical conversations
sentences.zh: 另一个群体则将那种行政或后勤性质的对话合并到

sentences.en: to set meetings, and what the doctor from that hospital told me
sentences.zh: 既定的会议中，那位来自该医院的医生告诉我，

sentences.en: is that they had a real hard time keeping people in that first group,
sentences.zh: 第一组人很难留住员工，

sentences.en: where in the second group people were much happier.
sentences.zh: 而在第二组中，大家要快乐得多。

sentences.en: So deep work doesn't necessarily mean I can sit, you know, half a day
sentences.zh: 所以深度工作并不一定意味着我可以坐上半天，

sentences.en: and just think about this one patient,
but just the ability to walk into a room and just think about that patient
sentences.zh: 而仅仅是走进一个房间就能只去想那个病人，

sentences.en: and not have to see 16 emails as you walk into the next room
sentences.zh: 不用在走进下一个房间时看到16封电子邮件

sentences.en: and have that eating away at your attention, that can really make a big difference.
sentences.zh: 并在那里蚕食你的注意力，这真的能产生巨大的差异。

sentences.en: You said that the people who were engaged in deep work ended up being happier.
sentences.zh: 你曾说过，从事深度工作的人最终会更快乐。

sentences.en: So it's not just a question of being more productive,
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是一个提高生产力的问题，

sentences.en: but you're making the case that deep work produces a kind of intrinsic reward
sentences.zh: 你还在证明，深度工作能带来一种内在的奖赏，

sentences.en: that doesn't come from being distracted?
sentences.zh: 这是分心所无法带来的？

sentences.en: And in fact, this caught me off guard when I was researching my book.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这在我在研究这本书时让我始料未及。

sentences.en: I ended up adding a chapter to the book that was not in the original proposal
sentences.zh: 我最终在书中增加了一个在最初提案中没有的章节

sentences.en: that was all about these findings I kept coming across
and these stories I kept coming across about deep living also just being good living.
sentences.zh: 以及我不断听到的关于深度生活同时也是美好生活的故事。

sentences.en: People who spend a larger proportion of their professional time concentrating intensely
sentences.zh: 把大部分职业时间用于高度集中精力

sentences.en: on a single high skill or high craft target tend to enjoy their work a lot more.
sentences.zh: 攻克单一高技能或高工艺目标的人，往往会从工作中获得更多的乐趣。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of different factors about why that might be true,
sentences.zh: 关于为什么会这样，有很多不同的因素，

sentences.en: but I, you know, ended by saying a deep life is a good life.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，我最后总结说，深度生活就是美好的生活。

sentences.en: And that's something I really believe in.
And it can take a knowledge work career and make it much more satisfying
sentences.zh: 它可以让知识型工作者的职业生涯变得更加令人满意，

sentences.en: than being in a persistent state of putting out fires and busy distraction.
sentences.zh: 而不是长期处于救火和纷扰分心的状态中。

sentences.en: Can you cite any professions where deep work is probably not called for
sentences.zh: 你能列举出哪些职业可能不需要深度工作，

sentences.en: and might even be a problem?
There's plenty of examples, I think, where deep work is probably not that relevant.
sentences.zh: 我认为有很多例子表明深度工作可能没有那么相关。

sentences.en: A couple of the common examples I give is actually,
sentences.zh: 我经常举的几个常见例子其实是，

sentences.en: I think being a CEO of a large company,
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一家大公司的首席执行官，

sentences.en: you're probably going to better serve your company or stockholders
sentences.zh: 你可能更好地为公司或股东服务的方式是

sentences.en: by being a decision engine for other people who are doing deep work.
sentences.zh: 充当其他从事深度工作的人的决策引擎。

sentences.en: Someone who people can come to, okay, what about this?
sentences.zh: 一个大家可以来找的人：好吧，这个怎么办？
我们在这里应该怎么做？

sentences.en: You can be a consistent source of the vision
sentences.zh: 你可以成为愿景的持续输出者，

sentences.en: and push these decisions in a consistent way.
sentences.zh: 并以一致的方式推动这些决策。

sentences.en: Another example is, let's say you're in what they would call here in D.C.,
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是，假设你在华盛顿特区所说的这行，

sentences.en: where really most of what you do is context and connections
sentences.zh: 这里你大部分的工作其实是背景和人脉，

sentences.en: and connecting the right people to the right other people
